A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BEP research. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison; v2's additional page results from reference reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLP and RNN classification experiments in Section 4, plus hyperparameter, binarization, mask-density, and backward-horizon analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses, including the benchmark results in Figure 2 and Table 1 and the appendix ablations.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1-3.5 and Appendix C retain the same architecture, prototype classifier, gated binary backpropagation, masked integer-weight updates, reinforcement, and BEP-TT procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same four MLP datasets, Sequential MNIST, and 30 UCR time-series datasets. Appendix D retains the same task coverage and test scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains Colombo et al. (2025) and Larq QAT with and without batch normalization. Table 1 retains the same two QAT variants for the RNN comparisons.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, preprocessing, model configurations, training budgets, validation procedures, metrics, and ablation settings in Section 4 and Appendix D are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix D retain the same analyses of gating, robustness margin, reinforcement probability, input binarization, mask density, and backward-horizon length. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report five-run MLP averages, three-fold cross-validation with three independent RNN runs, and three-run averages for the S-MNIST gating experiment. Error bars and tabulated uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2-8 and Tables 1-3 retain identical numerical results and plotted trends, including the benchmark comparisons and Appendix D ablations. No result entries or qualitative findings change.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations, Lemmas 1-3, Proposition 1, proofs in Appendices A-B, and prototype-construction objective in Appendix C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about a binary backpropagation analog, global credit assignment, end-to-end binary RNN training, and accuracy and computational benefits.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations remain unchanged. Section 4.5 retains the same limitations concerning architectures, classification-only evaluation, dataset scale, and network depth; future research directions are also retained.

D1.justification: Section 4, footnote 2 replaces the promise that the repository will be available upon acceptance with a concrete GitHub address for BEP. Other implementation disclosures are unchanged. Repository contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to QAT, local binary learning, and other optimization approaches are unchanged. References are repaginated without additions or removals.

P1.justification: v2 updates the publication header and affiliations and adds funding acknowledgements. The scientific prose, terminology, and main section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block is reformatted, Figure 1 moves from page 4 to page 3 with adjusted sizing and spacing, and references reflow onto an additional page. Result figures, tables, and appendix displays otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Replacing the future-release placeholder with a concrete repository address modestly improves code-access documentation. The scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged, so the gain is limited; the supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
